title: How do whales and dolphins talk to each other?

explain.say: Whales and dolphins live where sound travels far better than light, so they talk mainly with sound. The two big groups, toothed whales and baleen whales, do it differently.

draw.text: How do whales and dolphins talk to each other?

explain.say: Toothed whales use clicks and whistles. Each bottlenose dolphin has a signature whistle that works like a name, and sperm whales tap out rhythmic patterns of clicks called codas, which differ between family clans like dialects.

Baleen whales make deep moans, grunts and songs. Male humpbacks sing long songs of repeated themes; all the males in a region sing the same song, which slowly changes and can spread from one population to another.

Only male humpbacks sing, mostly in the breeding season, so the songs are probably about attracting mates or sizing up rivals. Scientists are still not certain, which makes it one of the ocean's great puzzles.

draw.question: Why do humpback whales sing?
draw.answer: Mostly linked to breeding, but nobody is sure

faq.a: In a way. Each bottlenose dolphin develops its own signature whistle early in life, and other dolphins copy it to call that individual, which then answers.
asks: Can dolphins call each other by name?

faq.a: Codas are short, rhythmic patterns of clicks that sperm whales exchange when they meet. Different family groups, called clans, use different sets of codas, like dialects.
asks: Do sperm whales talk in clicks?

faq.a: Only males sing, mostly during the breeding season, so the songs are probably linked to attracting females or competing with other males. Nobody knows for sure.

faq.q: How far can whale calls travel?
faq.a: The deep, low calls of blue and fin whales can travel hundreds of kilometres through the ocean, because low sounds lose little energy in water.
asks: Can whales hear each other across the ocean?
Why are whale calls so low?

faq.a: Yes, in a sense. Sperm whale clans use different coda dialects, killer whale pods have their own sets of calls, and humpbacks in one region share a song that differs from other regions.
asks: Do different whale groups sound different?

facts: Bottlenose dolphins respond when they hear a copy of their own signature whistle (King and Janik, 2013).
In 1996 and 1997 east Australian humpbacks switched to a new song brought by a few singers from the Indian Ocean population (Noad and colleagues, 2000).

quiz.say: Which whales sing long songs that change over the years?
quiz.show: Which whales sing long songs that change over the years?
quiz.why: Male humpbacks sing complex songs that all males in a region share and slowly change.

wrong.1: Sperm whales communicate with click codas, not songs.
wrong.2: Dolphins use whistles and clicks rather than long songs.

quiz.say: What does a dolphin's signature whistle work like?
quiz.show: What does a dolphin's signature whistle work like?
quiz.why: Each dolphin has its own whistle, and others copy it to call that dolphin.

wrong.1: It identifies one dolphin rather than warning of danger.
wrong.2: Dolphins find food with echolocation clicks, not their signature whistle.
